decisions.title: Modular monolith first, service extraction when evidence demands
decisions.context: A national healthcare platform must ship as one deployable before splitting services; premature microservices multiply operational cost across governorates without evidence.
decisions.decision: Adopt a modular monolith. Extract services only when measurement shows a real boundary (load, team, regulatory).
decisions.reason: One deployable unit minimizes governance, deployment, and rollback complexity during national pilot while preserving clear module boundaries for later extraction.
alternatives: Layered single module with no boundaries
trade_offs: Deployment blast radius spans the whole platform
Module boundaries must be enforced by review, not by process isolation
decisions.risk: Monolith grows into a ball of mud without boundary enforcement.
decisions.cost: Low — no extra infrastructure; requires review discipline.
decisions.rollback: Full revert of the module; extraction path remains open.
consequences: One deployable unit, clear module boundaries

decisions.title: FHIR R4 as the interoperability backbone
decisions.context: National health data must interoperate across ministries, directorates, hospitals, and laboratories.
decisions.decision: Adopt FHIR R4 resources as the canonical clinical contract, with HL7 adapters at the boundaries.
decisions.reason: FHIR R4 is the national-standard clinical contract; HL7 messaging is preserved for legacy analyzer and hospital bridges.
trade_offs: FHIR profiles require national conformance effort
HL7 v2 adapters add translation complexity
decisions.risk: Specification drift between national FHIR profiles and platform.
decisions.cost: Medium — conformance testing and profile management.
decisions.rollback: FHIR layer is additive; legacy data model retained.
consequences: FHIR R4 resources as the canonical clinical contract
HL7 messaging preserved at device and hospital boundaries

decisions.title: Multi-tenancy with tenant isolation at the data layer
decisions.context: Every governorate, directorate, hospital, and laboratory must operate independently without cross-tenant leakage.
decisions.decision: Enforce tenant isolation at the data layer: lab_id scoping through services and models, verified by the Reviewer.
decisions.reason: Regulatory and clinical safety require tenant-scoped access enforced in every query, not just at the UI.
trade_offs: Single schema requires disciplined scoping everywhere
Database-per-tenant multiplies operational cost
decisions.risk: A missing scoping filter leaks data across tenants.
decisions.cost: Low-to-medium — discipline enforced by tests and review.
decisions.rollback: Restore row-level scoping; no schema change.
consequences: Lab-level isolation enforced in every query

decisions.title: PostgreSQL + Redis as the platform data stack
decisions.context: Free, self-hosted, and operationally boring primitives support national deployment without vendor lock-in.
decisions.decision: Use PostgreSQL as the primary store and Redis for caching and the task queue; both replaceable behind interfaces.
decisions.reason: PostgreSQL and Redis are self-hosted, replaceable, and meet the Free/Open-Source/Self-Hosted-first constitution.
trade_offs: PostgreSQL requires migration discipline
Redis is memory-bound and needs eviction policy
decisions.risk: Operational tuning burden grows at national scale.
decisions.cost: Low — self-hosted OSS; operational expertise required.
decisions.rollback: Swap the cache/client behind existing interfaces.

decisions.title: Immutable audit log for clinical and administrative actions
decisions.context: Regulatory compliance (ISO 15189, CAP, CLSI) and national accountability require tamper-evident audit trails.
decisions.decision: Maintain an immutable, append-only audit log with verification capability for every clinical and administrative action.
decisions.reason: Clinical safety and regulatory certification demand append-only, verifiable records of every significant action.
trade_offs: Append-only storage grows unboundedly
Verification adds a small write-path cost
decisions.risk: Audit records could be tampered with if the store is compromised.
decisions.rollback: Immutable by design; no rollback, retention pruning only.

decisions.title: Offline-first operations for laboratory continuity
decisions.context: Laboratories in underserved governorates cannot depend on continuous connectivity.
decisions.decision: Design offline-first: local data capture, outbox-pattern synchronization, conflict-resolution policies.
decisions.reason: Clinical continuity requires local-first data capture with reliable synchronization when connectivity returns.
alternatives: Local terminals with nightly batch sync
trade_offs: Conflict resolution policies are complex
Offline capture adds validation latency
decisions.cost: Medium — sync engine and conflict policies.
decisions.rollback: Disable offline mode; revert to online-only.

decisions.title: Arabic-first user experience with RTL layout
decisions.context: The national platform serves Arabic-speaking clinical staff and citizens across Iraq.
decisions.decision: Deliver Arabic-first UI with dir="rtl" in frontend-v3, with internationalization for every user-facing string.
decisions.reason: Usability and national mandate require Arabic as the primary interface language with correct RTL rendering.
trade_offs: RTL layout requires careful component design
Translation keys add UI overhead
decisions.risk: Incomplete translation coverage for inactive contexts.
decisions.cost: Low-to-medium — i18n keying and RTL testing.
decisions.rollback: Flip locale preference; no schema change.

decisions.title: Centralized identity platform for all platform roles
decisions.context: Ministry, directorate, hospital, and laboratory hierarchies need a single identity authority with RBAC/ABAC.
decisions.decision: Adopt the centralized identity platform (NIAM) as the single authority with RBAC and ABAC authorization.
decisions.reason: A single identity authority keeps authorization consistent across the national hierarchy and avoids credential fragmentation.
trade_offs: Single authority is a high-value target
Federation adapters are required for national integration
decisions.risk: Identity coupling to the national federation roadmap.
decisions.cost: Medium — identity platform hardening and federation.
decisions.rollback: Adapter-based federation allows swapping the authority.

decisions.title: Event-driven integration between platform modules
decisions.context: Orders, results, notifications, and offline sync must react to domain events without hard coupling.
decisions.decision: Use a domain event bus with the outbox pattern for reliable event publishing across contexts.
decisions.reason: Domain events decouple contexts and enable the outbox pattern for reliable publishing.
trade_offs: Eventual consistency across consumers
Event schema versioning is required
decisions.rollback: Revert to synchronous calls for affected flows.
consequences: Domain events on a shared bus

decisions.title: National EHR compatibility (FHIR R4, SNDHS integration)
decisions.context: The platform must remain mergeable into future national health releases across all Iraqi governorates.
decisions.decision: Keep national EHR and SNDHS government integration on the roadmap with FHIR R4 contracts and gateway adapters.
decisions.reason: National compatibility is a core mission requirement; government integration gateways keep the platform sovereign.
alternatives: Closed platform with no national integration
trade_offs: Gateway adapters add surface area
National spec changes require adaptation
decisions.cost: High over 5 years — federation and compliance.
